exposure: infection with different Streptococcus agalactiae sequence types
outcome: invasiveness in human umbilical vein endothelial cells
invasiveness in human brain microvascular endothelial cells
invasiveness in human mammary epithelial cells
cohort: 80 pediatric Streptococcus agalactiae infection cases from a teaching hospital in Shanghai between 2009 and 2020
finding: The Ib/CC12 Streptococcus agalactiae strain is hypervirulent and multiresistant, leading to higher mortality in pediatric patients compared to other strains.
